title: WhatsApp Catalog Approval Time and How to Speed It Up
description: WhatsApp catalog approval time: what WhatsApp says, why some items wait longer, what to check if one is stuck and how to avoid getting items rejected.
h1: WhatsApp Catalog Approval Time: How Long It Takes and How to Speed It Up
answer: WhatsApp does not publish a fixed approval time for single catalog items. It says every item is checked first and shows to customers only after approval. For a new collection, WhatsApp says the check should take no more than 24 hours. Clear photos and complete details give an item the best chance of passing the first time.
waText: Hi OneCatalog, my WhatsApp catalog items are stuck in review. Can you help?

sections.h2: What is the normal WhatsApp catalog approval time?

blocks.p: Here is everything WhatsApp's own help pages say about timing. We checked them on 6 October 2026.

table.caption: WhatsApp catalog approval time, by what you add
head: What you add
What WhatsApp says
rows: A new item, with its photos or videos
Checked before customers can see it. No fixed time is given.
Checked, and should take no more than 24 hours.
You can ask for another review. If that fails, you can reply to ask for a third.
Changes to a connected Meta catalog
Should show in the WhatsApp Business app within 24 hours.

blocks.p: Be careful with websites that promise an exact number of minutes or hours for items. WhatsApp's help pages don't give one. When you see a short time quoted, it is someone's guess.

sections.h2: Why does approval take longer for some items?

blocks.p: WhatsApp checks every photo, video and item against its rules, the [Commerce Policy](https://www.whatsapp.com/policies/commerce-policy/). WhatsApp does not explain how long each check takes or why one item waits longer than another. These are the things you control:

ul: **Photos that look like adverts.** WhatsApp says the catalogue is for listing products, not for showing advertisements. A photo full of offer text or a price banner is more likely to get a closer look.
**Missing details.** Every item needs a unique title, at least one photo and a country of origin. An item without them will not save at all.

**Goods on the banned list.** Alcohol, tobacco, medicines and some other goods are not allowed in a WhatsApp catalogue at all. Our guide on [why WhatsApp rejects catalog items](/guides/whatsapp-catalog-rejected) lists them.

blocks.callout: **What we see with real shops:** owners often add a big batch of products the night before a sale and expect them all to show the next morning. Some are still waiting, and the sale post goes out with half a catalogue. Add new stock a few days before you plan to share it.

sections.h2: How to tell if an item is waiting, rejected or approved

blocks.p: Open the **Tools** tab and tap **Catalog**. Look at each item's photo.

table.caption: What each item status looks like
head: Status
What you see
Can customers see it?
rows: The item is in your catalogue with no mark
A red exclamation mark next to the photo

blocks.alt: WhatsApp Business catalogue list with one item showing a red exclamation mark
blocks.capture: Android. Tools > Catalog list with at least one rejected item (red exclamation mark) and one normal item.

blocks.p: Waiting and approved items look the same to you. The only sure test is to open your catalogue from someone else's phone. If they can see the item, it is approved.

sections.h2: What to check if an item is stuck in review

blocks.p: If an item still isn't showing to customers after a day or two, work through this list.

ol: Open your catalogue on a family member's phone. Make sure the item really is missing for customers.
Look for a red exclamation mark. If you see one, the item was rejected, not stuck. Go to the next section.
Check that the item isn't hidden. Our guide to a [WhatsApp catalogue not showing](/guides/whatsapp-catalog-not-showing) shows how to unhide items on Android and iPhone.
Update WhatsApp Business from the Play Store or App Store, then close and reopen the app.
If nothing works, contact WhatsApp support from the app. Tap **Settings**, then **Help and feedback**, **Help Center** and **Contact Us**.

blocks.p: WhatsApp says items are rejected for a variety of reasons, and points sellers to its Commerce Policy. The policy bans some goods outright, such as alcohol, tobacco, drugs and medical products, weapons and adult products. It also bans items that are misleading. Our guide on [why WhatsApp rejects catalog items](/guides/whatsapp-catalog-rejected) covers each reason and what to do about it.
If you think WhatsApp got it wrong, you can appeal:

ol: Type a short reason why the item is allowed.

blocks.capture: Android. A rejected catalogue item opened, with the 'Request another review' button visible.

sections.h2: How to speed up WhatsApp catalog approval

blocks.p: You can't make WhatsApp review faster. You can make sure each item passes the first time, so you don't lose days to a rejection and an appeal.

ul: Use a clear photo of the real product on a plain background. Leave out offer text, logos and price banners.
Give every item a unique name, like "Teak wood 3-seater sofa". Don't name ten items "Sofa".
Pick the country of origin every time. WhatsApp asks for it on every new or edited item.
Add items one at a time if saving fails. WhatsApp suggests this when changes don't save.
Add new stock a few days before you need to share it.
